1.title: Building Agents: Agent SDK, Custom Loops, Managed Agents and Hooks
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Building Agents: Agent S D K, Custom Loops, Managed Agents and Hooks. This module covers the skills agent construction with claude. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Three ways to construct an agent: a custom loop on the A P I (application programming interface), the Claude Agent S D K (software development kit), and Claude Managed Agents. What a harness is and what it must do. Deployment models: self-hosted versus Anthropic-hosted. Hooks for deterministic actions. Safety limits for runaway agents.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater's Overnight Investigator
1.text: Our running case is Tidewater Insurance. Tidewater's Overnight Investigator. The team wants an agent that investigates suspicious claims for hours, reads files, runs checks and writes a report. Requirements: compliance (data stays in Tidewater's cloud), audit logs, and a small team with little time for infrastructure.

1.title: Choosing How to Build
1.text: Choosing How to Build. The figure shows this: Three ways to build an agent: your own loop on the Messages A P I, the Agent S D K as a library you host, or Claude Managed Agents with a managed harness.

1.title: Choosing How to Build, continued
1.text: Choosing How to Build, continued. Custom loop on the Messages A P I. What you get: Direct model access, fine-grained control. You provide: The loop, tool execution, context management, retries, permissions, logging. Choose it when: Unusual requirements, or you must control every call. Claude Agent S D K. What you get: The same agent loop and built-in tools as Claude Code, as a Python or Type Script library, with subagents, hooks, sessions and permissions. You provide: Hosting and operations. Choose it when: You want a proven harness but control over where it runs.

1.title: Choosing How to Build, continued
1.text: Choosing How to Build, continued. Claude Managed Agents (beta). What you get: A pre-built agent harness on managed infrastructure with sandboxes, built-in prompt caching and compaction. You provide: Agent definition and application integration. Choose it when: Long-running or asynchronous work with little infrastructure effort. Exam tip: "Long-running, asynchronous, minimal infrastructure" to Managed Agents. "Own the loop and every call" to custom loop. "Claude's harness, hosted by us" to Agent S D K.

1.title: The harness
1.text: The harness. The harness is everything around the model: the loop, tool execution, permissions, context management (pruning, compaction), retries and limits, logging, and session state. Building your own harness gives control but costs effort and risk; the S D K and Managed Agents supply one.

1.title: Agent SDK Essentials
1.text: Agent S D K Essentials. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Agent SDK Essentials, continued
1.text: Agent S D K Essentials, continued. Built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, web tools) and custom tools or M C P (Model Context Protocol) servers can be added; subagents are defined in code or files. The loop ends when the model replies with no tool calls; a result message carries the outcome (success or a limit such as maximum turns or budget). Permissions: allow lists, deny lists and permission modes control what runs without approval. Sessions can be resumed or forked (see the Architect course for detail). Exam tip: Ask who should run the harness: you (custom loop or Agent S D K) or Anthropic (Managed Agents), then weigh control against effort.

1.title: Managed Agents and Deployment Models
1.text: Managed Agents and Deployment Models. The figure shows this: Managed Agents in four concepts: Agent, Environment, Session and Events.

1.title: Managed Agents and Deployment Models, continued
1.text: Managed Agents and Deployment Models, continued. Agent. The model, system prompt, tools, M C P servers and skills. Environment. Where sessions run: an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox, or a self-hosted sandbox on your infrastructure. Session. A running agent instance doing a task. Events. The messages between your application and the agent (user turns, tool results, status updates). Self-hosted versus Anthropic-hosted: an Anthropic-managed sandbox minimizes infrastructure work; a self-hosted sandbox keeps execution in your own environment for compliance or data-residency needs. Managed Agents provide caching and compaction in the harness. Sessions are stateful and their transcripts persist until you delete them.

1.title: Managed Agents and Deployment Models, continued
1.text: Managed Agents and Deployment Models, continued. Claude Managed Agents is a beta feature on the Claude A P I (and available with some differences on partner platforms). Check the overview page for current models, platforms and limits. As of eight November two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Hooks and Safety Limits
1.text: Hooks and Safety Limits. Hooks are code that runs at fixed points of the agent loop, outside the model: before a tool runs (Pre Tool Use: allow, deny or rewrite), after a tool returns (Post Tool Use: log, transform), on prompt submit, on stop and more. Use hooks for deterministic actions: block destructive commands, enforce policy, redact secrets from tool output, write an audit log. Prompts alone cannot guarantee these. Safety limits for runaway agents: maximum turns, budget caps, timeouts, allow and deny lists, and sandboxing.

1.title: Hooks and Safety Limits, continued
1.text: Hooks and Safety Limits, continued. The figure shows this: Hooks act at fixed points of the loop and give deterministic guarantees; limits cap turns, budget and time. Exam tip: A rule that must always hold (never run a destructive command, never log a secret) is a hook or permission rule, not a prompt sentence.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Build options: Custom loop (full control), Agent S D K (Claude's harness as a library), Managed Agents (managed harness, long-running work). Harness: Loop, tool execution, permissions, context management, retries, logging, state. Managed Agents: Agent, Environment (cloud or self-hosted sandbox), Session, Events; beta. Hosting: Anthropic-managed equals least effort; self-hosted equals compliance and residency. Hooks: Pre Tool Use (allow, deny, rewrite), Post Tool Use (log, transform); deterministic. Limits: Max turns, budget, timeouts, permissions, sandboxing.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Tidewater needs an agent that works for hours asynchronously with very little infrastructure effort. Which option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Managed Agents provide a ready harness and sandboxes for long-running, asynchronous work.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team must keep agent code execution inside its own cloud for compliance. Which deployment model fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Self-hosted sandboxes run on your infrastructure for compliance and residency needs.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What does the Claude Agent S D K give a developer? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The S D K packages Claude's own harness as a Python or Type Script library.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which task is best handled by a hook rather than a prompt instruction? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. A destructive-action guarantee needs deterministic enforcement outside the model.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An agent occasionally loops far too long and costs rise. Which controls help most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Limits cap runaway behavior regardless of what the model decides.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What belongs to the harness of an agent? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The harness is everything around the model that makes it work as an agent.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. In Managed Agents, which concept defines where sessions run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The environment is the cloud or self-hosted sandbox in which sessions execute.

1.title: Practice Question 8
1.text: Question eight. Why might a team build a custom loop on the Messages A P I instead of using the S D K? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. A custom loop trades effort for full control.

1.title: Practice Question 9
1.text: Question nine. Select two. Which two are valid uses of hooks in an agent? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. Hooks intercept calls and results deterministically; they do not choose models, guarantee reasoning or replace permissions.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all nine answers. Question one: B. Question two: B. Question three: D. Question four: C. Question five: D. Question six: D. Question seven: D. Question eight: B. Question nine: B and D. In the next module, we continue the course.
